Compare projectable clustering methods with common participant subsamples

Source: R/ClusterMethodBenchmark.R
CompareClusterMethodStability.Rd

Fits each requested candidate on the same full reference cohort, then on identical 90% participant subsamples. Every refit is projected to the full complete reference cohort before participant-level agreement is calculated. This makes ARI comparable across clustering methods rather than comparing only participants retained by a particular refit.

Usage

CompareClusterMethodStability(
  data,
  variables,
  candidates = NULL,
  stability_resamples = 10L,
  stability_seed = 934522L,
  stability_cores = NULL,
  subsample_fraction = 0.9,
  keep_models = FALSE
)

Arguments

data

A data frame containing the clustering variables.

variables

Numeric clustering variables.

candidates

A candidate specification data frame. NULL constructs the planned SOM/Mclust, Mclust, K-means, HDBSCAN, and Ward-plus-random-forest candidate set. See DefaultClusterBenchmarkCandidates().

stability_resamples

Number of common 90% subsample refits. Defaults to 10 for screening.

stability_seed

Seed used to generate the shared participant draws.

stability_cores

Optional number of parallel workers.

subsample_fraction

Proportion of complete reference participants retained in each refit.

keep_models

Logical; retain full-data reference models in the screen result. Defaults to FALSE to avoid holding one large model per candidate. Confirmation always retains its selected projectable models.

Value

A ClusterMethodStabilityBenchmark object with decision_table, replicates, shared subsamples, participant_inclusion, and full-data models. With keep_models = FALSE, models is an empty list.

Details

Candidate rows use Method values "som_mclust", "mclust", "kmeans", "hdbscan", or "ward_rf". K-based candidates require Classes; mixture candidates also require Model. SOM candidates use NodeWeighting, SOM_XDim, SOM_YDim, and SOM_Topology; HDBSCAN uses MinPts and Epsilon; and Ward-plus-RF uses WardN and RF_Trees. Full benchmarks near 20,000 participants can be slow and memory-intensive. HDBSCAN and Ward + RF allocate pairwise structures and are automatically serial under the memory policy; use a small, reviewed candidate table for large cohorts.
